newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK PRESIDENT IN FAVOUR OF REFERENDA - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK PRESIDENT IN FAVOUR OF REFERENDA - PAPER.

text.p: Slovak President Michal Kovac welcomed a court ruling paving the way for a referendum on whether to hold direct presidential elections and urged citizens to vote "yes".

"This ruling of the court could help so far undecided citizens to reconsider their doubts... and take part in the referendum," Kovac said in an interview with Thursday's edition of the independent daily Pravda.
Premier Vladimir Meciar's government submitted a proposal to the court to declare the referendum unconstitutional and suspended preparations for the vote.
The referendum on the direct election of the president is due to be held on May 23-24 alongside another on whether Slovakia should join NATO.
The referendum was seen as an attempt to prevent Meciar from assuming presidential powers when Kovac, an avowed political foe of the premier, steps down at the end of his term next March.
Parliament currently elects the Slovak president.
Kovac reiterated his support both for the change to the constitution and for NATO membership and urged citizens to follow his lead.
"I will vote for Slovakia's membership in NATO and also for direct presidential elections," he said.

Slovakia, independent since Czechoslovakia split in two in 1993, has applied to be among the first new members of NATO, but its chances appear thin after Western criticism of the pace of its democratic reforms.

Kovac hinted that he would ignore questions on whether nuclear warheads or foreign military units could be deployed on Slovak territory, which, the opposition says, were deliberately phrased to make people vote against membership and give political cover to Meciar's government.
"These two (questions) are not so serious at the moment...but I leave this up to every citizen," he said.
